JUDGMENT Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/

1 The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 26.03.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- JC-3849, from Magadipalya Circle side towards Nagasandra side in front of Sri.Shaneshwara Swamy Temple, Manavahalli, Koppa Village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District.
At that time one Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-N-6521 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident the petitioner fell down and has sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to A.C.Giri Hospital, Belluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and discharged with an advice continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 30 years as on the date of accident.
He was working as Labour work and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent No.1, who drive his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-N-6521.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said vehicle
thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.2 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
7. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till realization.
8. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsels and filed their written statement on behalf of respondent No.2 by denying the entire petition averments.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/
2

Further denied the age of the petitioner, avocation, income, injuries sustained, treatment underwent by the petitioner, disability certificate obtained by the petitioner, medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
9. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents in total as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.

The respondent No.2 company has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked 7 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.7 and case was posted for arguments.
10. Heard the arguments on both side and perused the materials on record.
11. Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous in- juries due to the actionable negligent driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-N- 6521 by its driver, in RTA took place on 26.03.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., in front of Sri.Shaneshwaraswamy Tem- ple, Magadipalya, Manavahalli, Koppa Village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
12. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative

;
 Issue No.2 :

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per the final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
13. The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 26.03.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JC-3849,
from Magadipalya Circle side towards Nagasandra side in front of Sri.Shaneshwara Swamy Temple,
Manavahalli, Koppa Village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District.
At that time one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-N-6521 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident the petitioner fell down and has sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.

Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/
3 14.

The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
15. By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents in total on his behalf.
In his chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offender vehicle.
16. The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
17. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
18. The Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked 7 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.7.
RW.1 has reiterated the contents of written statement filed by the respondent No.1 in his examination in chief.

RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for petitioner during the course of cross- examination of petitioner she had admitted that she has deposed her evidence on the basis of documents submitted by the private investigating officer of her company and has not participated in the said private investigation held on behalf of company.
She does not have any personal knowledge about the case.
The policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of our insured vehicle.

19. The Learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has addressed detail arguments stating that the DL of the insured vehicle driver is in question and the private investigating officer on behalf of respondent company has conducted investigation and has submitted CD in this regard.
It is further argued that the fractures/injuries are unite and the doctor who has assessed the disability is not a treated doctor therefore prayed to accept the contention of the respondent.
However, the above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1 offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- N-6521.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by him.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.

In support of the case petitioner has come up with Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/
4 various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head

, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate which are marked as per Ex.P.5.
As per the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
The Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital from 26.03.2022 to 01.04.2022 for a period of 6 days.
These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Center, but the doctor is not examined by petitioner.
Without the examination of the doctor it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

In number of Judgments delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court it is highlighted that i) In a motor vehicle accident case, where a doctor was not examined court may award "global compensation" which is typically a lower amount due to the lack of concrete medical evidence to support the extent of injuries often resulting in a reduced compensation package compared to cases with proper medical documentation.
Due to lack of crucial medical evidence from the doctors only covers minimal damages or pain and sufferings.

ii). Courts may reason that without a proper medical examination, it is difficult to accurately assess the extent of the disability and the resulting loss of income or future prospectus leading to a lower over all compensation award.
iii). Even if a doctor was not examined, the court may still consider the visible injuries or the severity of the accident when determining the compensation amount.
iv). The court may rely on the claimant's own testimony regarding their injuries and limitations but this may be less persuasive without supporting medical evidence.

Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/
5 v).

Some cases has seen tribunals award a nominal compensation amount such as a few thousand rupees, when a claimant failed to present a doctor's examination report, highlighting the importance of medical documentation in such cases.
vi) Not examining the doctor significantly weakens the plaintiff's case as it make it difficulty to establish the standard of care that was breached and the patient's injury.
vii) The plaintiff bears the burden of proving medical negligence and failing to examine the treating doctor can make it challenging to meet this standard.
viii) Several Indian Court cases have highlighted the issue of not examining the treating doctor, resulting in significantly reduced compensation awards.

ix) Even if a court does award compensation, the amount will likely be lower due to factors like the severity of the injury, availability of other medical evidence and the plaintiff's contribution to the situation.

In Sunitha V/s Rajasthan State Transport Corporation dated 15.02.2019 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that, non examination of "best witness" in motor accident claim cases is not fatal and also not to find fault with non examination of some best witnesses.

entities.text: Sunitha V/s Rajasthan State Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court to the case on hand it is observed that though non examination of the doctor by the petitioner is not fatal to the case but without the assessment of the disability by the doctor it is impossible to believe that the petitioner has sustained the injuries narrated in the petition.
Thereby the petitioner is not entitled to compensation towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a Labour and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove the income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.517/-.
As per the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient for 6 days and after discharge from the hospital there must be necessary to take bed rest for at least 24 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.31,020/- (30 days X 517 = Rs.15,510 + 15,510).
(B) Medical expenditure:-

The petitioner has incurred Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance,
medical treatment, attendant and nursing care expenses.
The petitioner has placed reliance on medical bills.

On perusal of the same it is arrived at Rs.23,940/- as per Ex.P.9.

6

sentences.text: (C) Future medical expenditure
The petitioner has not claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
Therefore the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under this head.
(D) Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 6 days with extended follow up treatment.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance to meet the treatment.
Wound certificate Ex.P6 shows injuries and patient would have received help from family members are friends to get admitted at the hospital.

In Pradeep B. Siddarameshwara v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Dated:10.12.2014 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that "on account of non-examination of doctor and assessment of disability by doctor being not available on record, Tribunal has proceeded to award global compensation of Rs.3,000/-, which is abysmally on the lower side.

entities.text: Pradeep B. Siddarameshwara v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that claimant had sustained fracture of left ring finger and due to same he has undergone pain and suffering, this Court is of the considered view that additional compensation of Rs.20,000/-, if awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

Said additional global compensation is awarded taking into consideration the nature of injury, which covers the head of 'loss of income daring laid up period', 'pain and suffering', 'loss of amenities' and disability that has been sustained by claimant."

In Devaraju V/s Sharad Sharma dated:
15.03.2011 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that "Material submissions probabalise, accident is not disputed actionable negligence is not disputed, wound certificate is marked.
Wound certificate reflects two fractures.
It is believed by the tribunal.
It is not the quantum of evidence, it is quality is the criteria.
Compensation awarded at Rs. 12,000/- is on lesser side.

So it is enhanced to global amount of Rs.
40,000/- difference of Rs. 28,000/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit"

Therefore in absence of proof, it would be reasonable to award conveyance charges,
attendance and special diet of Rs.25,000/- each.
In total the petitioner is entitle for Rs.75,000/- under this head.

(a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained injuries as on the date of accident.

The said accidental injuries have caused lot of pain to suffer in the future Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93087197/
7 life span.

entities.text: Suresha .K.M vs Mahadev .S.M on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pain and suffering would be categorized as a non-pecuniary loss as it is incapable of being arithmetically calculated.

Therefore, when compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering, special circumstances of the claimant have to be taken into account including the victim's age, the unusual deprivation the victim has suffered, the effect thereof on his or her future life.

Like wise, in the case of Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Devaraju V/s Sharad Sharma dated: 15.03.2011 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177 the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

entities.text: Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Devaraju V/s Sharad Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above formula to the case on hand and by considering the nature of the injuries caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
This includes a variety of matters such as the inability to walk, run or sit, etc.
This shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of the personal life and amenities of life.
In T.Murthy V/s Zabiulla Dated 08.01.2016
Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that "I find that the tribunal has committed an error in not considering Ex.P.8 wound certificate and non examination of doctor.
For having suffered grievous injury in the road accident which has been proved before the tribunal, I am inclined to grant another Rs.25,000/- global compensation".
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.2,59,960/- which is just and proper.
22. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,59,960/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
